answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from requiring each participant to stake a unique geological proof of work that cannot be cheaply duplicated. Imagine agents must carve a personal marker into canyon walls of basalt and shale strata, then submit a verifiable sample of the layered rock that only a single continuous effort can produce. Because forging fresh basalt-shale sequences at scale is expensive, mass identity creation becomes impractical while honest agents still participate freely.
